strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations (one initial sum + 7 dependent iterations) with local compute (abs, mean, scale) between each. Total ~8 collective dispatches with full 4096-element payload each time. Represents the reference pattern with no optimization—high latency due to serial dependency chain but straightforward correctness.

strategies.name: Fused Local Compute Between Collectives
strategies.desc: Same 8 all-reduce structure but aggressively fuses all local operations (abs, mean, multiply, divide) into single kernel launches between collectives to minimize host-device round-trips. Still 8 collective dispatches but reduces local overhead. Trades implementation complexity for lower non-communication latency while maintaining identical communication volume.

strategies.name: Block-Parallel Pipelined All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Splits the 8 blocks spatially and issues separate all-reduce calls per block (or small block groups) to enable network pipelining across the dependency chain. Total ~56-64 collective dispatches (8 blocks × 7-8 rounds) with 512-element payloads. Trades increased dispatch count for potential overlap of communication phases across blocks, beneficial if network can pipeline small messages.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction Tree
strategies.desc: Exploits multi-node topology by performing intra-node reductions (e.g., across local devices) followed by inter-node all-reduce, repeated 8 times. Uses reduce-scatter + all-gather or node-local optimized paths. ~16 collective dispatches (8 rounds × 2-level hierarchy). Reduces cross-node bandwidth pressure at cost of more complex two-phase coordination per iteration.

strategies.name: Speculative Parallel Launch with Barriers
strategies.desc:
Launches all 8 all-reduce collectives asynchronously upfront with explicit wait/barrier synchronization and host-side dependency management, allowing runtime to optimize scheduling. Still 8 dispatches but removes host-side serialization bottleneck between rounds. Trades predictability for potential runtime reordering benefits, requires careful buffer management to avoid race conditions on intermediate results.

def r61b_dd_absmean_p512_d8_fn(x, rank, world_size, num_devices,
                 cores_per_device, xm, torch, num_nodes=1):
    S = 512
    B = 8
    dtype = x.dtype
    
    # Initial all-reduce
    s = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, x)
    
    # Reshape once for all operations
    s_view = s.view(B, S)
    
    # 6 iterations of the pattern
    for iteration in range(6):
        # Compute absolute values once and reuse
        abs_s = s_view.abs()
        
        # Compute mean along dimension 1
        mean_abs = abs_s.mean(dim=1)
        
        # Compute factor
        f = 1.0 + mean_abs
        
        # Expand factor for broadcasting
        f_expanded = f.unsqueeze(1)
        
        # Scale
        buf_view = s_view * f_expanded
        
        # All-reduce
        buf = buf_view.reshape(-1)
        acc = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, buf)
        
        # Reshape and unscale
        acc_view = acc.view(B, S)
        s_view = acc_view / (world_size * f_expanded)
    
    # 7th iteration: similar pattern but without final unscaling
    abs_s = s_view.abs()
    mean_abs = abs_s.mean(dim=1)
    f = 1.0 + mean_abs
    f_expanded = f.unsqueeze(1)
    buf_view = s_view * f_expanded
    buf = buf_view.reshape(-1)
    
    acc = xm.all_reduce(xm.REDUCE_SUM, buf)
    
    # Final division by world_size only
    acc = acc / world_size
    
    return acc
